subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw core expose managed per-agent plugin installs now, and if so what install-record identity, uninstall/update/discovery, and plugin trust semantics must ship together?
rationale: The PR changes public CLI and persisted plugin lifecycle state in a security-sensitive area, and the durable contract cannot be chosen safely from code review alone.

options.title: Complete lifecycle contract before merge
options.body: Require one coherent implementation covering scoped install identity, uninstall, update/index/discovery, doctor/docs, and security proof before exposing `--agent`.

options.title: Pause for design review
options.body: Keep the PR open but blocked while maintainers decide whether this belongs in core and what guarantees per-agent plugin roots need.

options.title: Accept install-only experiment
options.body: Merge the partial install surface intentionally, accepting that operators may hit known cleanup, update, and trust-boundary gaps.

recommendation.title: Complete lifecycle contract before merge
recommendation.body: Require one coherent implementation covering scoped install identity, uninstall, update/index/discovery, doctor/docs, and security proof before exposing `--agent`.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across plugin install roots, command helpers, and lifecycle behavior affected by this decision.
